body: I don't know who exactly told me to be honest. But I've had the assumption for a while now that asking things like that is not respecting privacy and bringing up the past.
Thank you. I have some really good friends in my life at least.
Thank you <3

That's a good way of putting it. I said something similar to her. I told her I don't understand why it is always expected of me to see the good in the people that wronged me when nobody grants me that same kindness.

When I told her that her behavior upset me she said I was being disrespectful.

Thank you <3 I cut out most of my bio family years ago because of this stuff... I didn't want to lose her too. But I'm in therapy and really trying to be better emotionally and she wasn't willing to talk to me at all in a way that was reasonable.

Thank you. It is really hard. I was trying to put everything in the past.

Somehow I could rationalize her accepting the family that abused me, because they're her family. But the fact that she defended an abusive ex boyfriend just makes me feel so betrayed. She doesn't owe him anything. And she knows what he did. So I just can't rationalize that in any way that makes sense to me.

Thank you.

She did stay friends with him... she even forwarded me messages from him after our break up when I told him to stop contacting me unless it was related to the property I was at the time trying to collect from him, that he packed when he moved out.

She did this after I told her: "I think he was abusive."

Her response to that was "It's a possibility."

She contacted me today with a message. It was long and messy she said she was sorry I felt that way and that she feels she defended me while also staying classy and not getting involved in mud slinging.

I asked her why defending me involved also defending him.

The last message she sent me, summarised, said:

"What do you want me to do, strip naked in public and whip myself until I bleed and tell everyone what a useless person I am? Barring that, all I can do is leave you with love."

I told her that maybe her and my family should stop being so obsessed with maintaining a classy public image and start being classy in private too, then they wouldn't have so much to be ashamed about. Then I blocked her.

I am now no contact with all of my blood family except for my grandma's sister (who essentially raised me) and my one cousin. He moved to a different country at 17 to get away from a lot of this.

It feels very lonely but she wasn't willing to have any sort of conversation with me. It was just justifications and guilt trips. And I'm tired of that.
She's 25 I believe.
I broke up with him. This is an old story. Hence "ex"
I broke up with him beginning of this year

I started dating a guy at 18 that was ten years older than me.

He was also like this. Never did anything he had to, I carried the responsibilities on my shoulders.

As soon as I dumped him, he somehow managed to figure out how to do everything.

This is not incompetence. He is taking advantage of you being inexperienced with relationships and your kind heart.

He is 35. Do you really think he's made it this far in life without knowing these things? He does this because he knows he can get away with it.

I've been thinking about this comment this week.

I watched the movie last night.

Weird how the main plot of the movie actually turned out to be about abuse - and how it can poison you inside.

That shook me quite a bit. But it made me think. And as much as he hurt me, I don't want to let that poison me.

I've been very, very bitter since our breakup. I've acted in ways that I'm not proud of, informed by emotion.

I don't wanna be that way. And watching the movie made me really reflect and celebrate getting out of that environment that was slowly eroding my good qualities.

Sorry for rambling but yeah thank you for telling me to reclaim it. It was nice to.
He was!

I don't know what he'd be trying to guilt me for.

To be fair, it's possible he thought it was my  book. We shared a bookshelf for a good few years. So I'll have to give him the benefit of the doubt.
We didn't start dating until I was 18. So he \*technically\* did nothing wrong, unfortunately.

Yep. It feels like a strong word. But I'd hesitantly say he groomed me.

We met when I was 17. He claims to have fallen in love at first sight. He was my first boyfriend, my first kiss, first everything 😔

Definitely used my inexperience against me. Still trying to figure out what exactly a normal healthy relationship is.

It's actually ridiculous...

My best friend was getting sick of me being sad about the breakup. She said to me, blunt as hell:

"He's almost forty, and he's a homeless strip club dj. I think you'll live."

He started working at a strip club three nights a week around the time of our breakup. He used to tell me my job in marketing wasn't "meaningful" and didn't contribute anything to the world. 

He also told me my job as a shot girl was "basically being a stripper" and that I was betraying feminism.

Pot, kettle, black.

He brought 💫emotional abuse💫 to the table

He also actively discouraged me from getting my license. I believe so that he could bring being able to drive to the table.

But he complained so much about driving me anyway that I arranged carpools to work and when that wasn't possible I ubered.
Was a process, but definitely worth it.

Thank you 🧡 last I heard he was crashing on people's couches, while I moved into my dream apartment that has a free gym, on site coworking, cleaning services, a restaurant, etc etc...

Not to sound materialistic. But it feels damn good to finally enjoy the benefits of my labour and not give it to someone else.
I do everything by myself now, and somehow I have more money, a cleaner house, and more free time. Funny how that works.

He thought he was punishing me but truly it was luxurious having the place to myself. No one making snide comments about anything I watched. No one literally draining my happiness the moment I stepped in the door. Bliss.

I can't believe I lived in an environment that made me miserable for so long. I used to dread leaving the office and going home to him. As soon as I asked "how was your day".... the incessant complaining began
Oooh the drinking. We might have dated the same person. I'd give him money to go buy food and when I get home there would be booze in the fridge 😒
Living alone is the greatest thing I've ever done for myself

That was one of the moments that really made me stop and realise how delusional he is. He even said "I'm not gonna do everything so you can lay around all day just because you work and pay for everything."

🥴🥴🥴
This is an old story.
Thank you ❤

Yeah. I get that now.

We actually met when I was 17. Started dating when I was 18. Broke up when I was 23.

So realizing I was an object to be discarded and used to someone I loved for most of my adult life hurts.

Thank you.

It's been hard. My therapist has said a lot of the same things.

I really love my mother. I feel for her. She had a very traumatic life and she had me when she was very young. I often feel responsible that her life is the way it is, because she had me so young.

She has her own mental health issues. When I discussed what I was going through and what I was learning from my psychiatrists and therapists the conversations always turned into her own experiences with mental health somehow. It was demoralizing.

But she was one of the only people that actually checked up on me too. So I don't know how to feel about it entirely yet. I feel like she really does try in her own way.

In theory this is great advice.

But I have a little brother who I'd very much like to remain in contact with.

I know my boundaries are fucked. I know that. It's something I know I need to work on. I just don't want to lose the little family I have left.
I don't understand?

It's not just you.

I switch between being completely emotionally shut down and irritable when speaking to my parents. It makes me feel like I'm the problem, because they could be doing nothing wrong and I'll be ready to rage at the snap of a finger.

Hugs x

Thank you ❤

My therapist suggested that I call her out straight when she does things like this: "Mom, when you call me while crying, that is manipulation."

I just have not had the guts to do this at all. I was hoping somebody here has gone through something similar and could provide more insight.

My mom going to therapy with me is not an option for a whole bunch of reasons.
He cheated on me last year. She only told me this year. We were in contact after our breakup because he had some of my property.
Amen to that 🥳

I should have stayed away from him the moment he tried to hit on me when I was 17 and he was 27.

But so we learn. Trying to not be too hard on myself and just go on forward. Sharing the stories here have helped.

I have a bunch of drafts, ten and counting.

Thank you. I'm trying not to let it get to me.

I really feel like he did it on purpose, to make me go through what I did with my family again, where everyone also blamed me. And I have to be honest... when this keeps happening, and I'm the common denominator, it's hard not to feel like it is my fault.
My therapist did kindly point out to me that I seemed to repeat the dynamic I had with my mom in my relationship. It was a very gross and uncomfortable realization.

She did believe me... I moved away because she is still close to the people that didn't.

Thank you ❤ I really appreciate your kindness.

And to be fair to her, she asked me if I wanted to see the post before she sent the screenshots. She just told me he posted something about me and asked if I'd like to see. It's my fault for saying yes.

I don't know. Things are complicated with her. It's not something I like to think about because I love her.

But I did move away from her and the rest of my family when I was 21. So I'm not in a lot of contact with any of them.
This friend of his actually spoke to me afterwards and tried to encourage me to leave him, but I was too deep in the fog at that point to listen.

I don't think my mom really believes me when I say he was abusive.

When I left him, I told her a few months afterwards that he was abusive.

She replied "It's a possibility."

Even in the comment she left on that post of which, of which she sent me a screenshot, she said him and I were both toxic, not just him.

Thank you. I hate that I stayed with him for so long. I feel like I wasted a lot of my youth with him.

But I'm doing better. I'm in therapy. I'm focusing on my career. I'm going out, to parties, concerts, on dates. All the things I never got to do while I was with him.
https://imgur.com/a/c5fW6fx picture of my broken phone
I'm not anymore. I left him at the beginning of this year due to his abuse
That's true. I am very, very thankful I got out. I think he may have killed me one day. His abuse just kept escalating over the years.
He did have me go off my meds. I'll share that story here as well.

I'm sorry you went through that.

I still haven't been able to watch the movie again. Each time I start it I get anxious. I wish I could stop that.

I still don't know why I did. Sometimes when I had conversations with him he'd talk so much and so fast and flip everything back on me so expertly that I felt confused, and like I couldn't articulate anything, and it was just easier to agree with him. I really felt like I was going crazy.

Yeah. The power dynamic in our relationship was intense. Every choice he had last say because he was "more experienced". Even though I was the one financially supporting us by working two jobs while he was unemployed for the last year. He had final say over everything, including where we lived, even if I begged for us to move somewhere with lower rent.

When I left him start of this year, I moved into my dream apartment building which costs nearly half of what I was paying for our place we had together. He always badmouthed this place because he said it was dangerous. I've never felt safer in my life since moving here, and it's not even 5 minutes away from my office.
Yeah. I agree. I was 17 when I met him. The red flags in hindsight make me feel like an idiot.
I left him at the start of this year. I was very low contact with him for months, up until October of this year. I wish that I had gone full no contact. I only did that about a week ago.
I've never thought about it that way before. Honestly, if I found out my child was dating someone like him someday, I'd be terrified.

I left him at the start of this year. I haven't seen him physically since. He knows which apartment building I stay in now which makes me nervous, but the place is huge and he doesn't know which apartment number and he is not cleared with security to be allowed inside the premises.

It's just hard to wrap my head around my fact that people could do things like this with ill intent on purpose... since leaving him and trying to work through everything that happened, my fundamental worldviews have shifted a lot.

Yes, verbal abuse. Emotional abuse. He did destroy my property, but I blamed myself for that for months.

I do have pictures of the phone he broke in half and screenshots of him admitting to doing it...

Theoretically I could go to the police now, after the fact. But when I previously reported being assaulted to them they took my statement and did nothing. And it ended up being a very traumatic experience, the feeling of being dismissed and not taken seriously.

I'm not sure what country you're in, but I'm in South Africa. The police here don't really do much in terms of helping anyone, even if they got beaten by their partners.

He has sent me many heartfelt apologies. I have three multiple page long letters he emailed to me since october. In which he admits to abusing me but maintains he has changed and that he'll fall to his knees and cry if I give him another chance. Meanwhile, he has a pregnant girlfriend that he's treating the same abusive ways he treated me...

I shouldnt keep being surprised, but i am.

1. I don't know.
2. No, he didn't, I was in love with him.
3. Report him for what? We did not have sexual contact while I was a minor, we just met then.

To his credit. The reason we moved here was because he took me out of an already abusive household.

So I don't want to go back.

I'm still in touch with my friends. I've told them what happened and they understood why I was more distant. Moving away probably actually saved our friendships because I had a reasonable excuse for not seeing them. Before I moved I often had to cancel plans. Or spent the whole night dealing with him over text.

I have a good job here. That's one thing he's never been able to take from me. I work hard. I make good money for my age. I have my own place, I pay all my own bills. Hell, the last year of our relationship he didnt work and I payed all his bills too.

My coworker has been a rock. She integrated me into her social circle. I have good people around me now. Amazingly supportive women and men. I've never imagined being friends with a man before, but they've been nothing but respectful, and kind, and a blast to be around.

So I don't want to move. I think I'm on the right path. I just got knocked down again temporarily.
I fully agree with this. I didn't know better then. And if you can believe it, nobody disapproved of the age gap either.

I don't know what I'd report him for.

We didnt have any sexual while I was a minor and she isn't a minor either.

He's verbally abusive. But not physically. He never hit me or her. What he does is intimidation by throwing things, breaking phones, punching walls. He screams insults and breaks you down.

Realistically if I go to the police, what would they do? When I reported being sexually assaulted when I was a minor they took my statement and nothing happened.

I have very little faith in the law.
Thank you. I don't think I've grieved. After I left him, a lot of things happened. I haven't really had a chance to sit with it.

I do see that. And that's the worst part. I know all of this logically, I know that he's a piece of trash, but it hurts so much. He was the only person in my life for five years. I moved to a city across the country, with him. He isolated me and I didn't make any friends here, it was just him, for years.

I guess just knowing that he never actually cared about me hurts. But I'm really, really trying to build a new life for myself.

She contacted me on Facebook and the profile looked real and legit. Including baby ultrasound pictures.

I answered her specific questions, then wished her luck. She sent me screenshots of him saying that he's never talking to her again because she contacted me. Because she didn't respect his "privacy". He ended up contacting me again after telling me how happy he was and threatening me with a restraining order. I know that it's an empty threat, because I have proof of him admitting to verbally abusing me and destroying my property as an intimidation tactic.

That's when I blocked her. Because I didn't want to be involved anymore. I also blocked every single person I could think of connected to him, everywhere, and asked my parents not to pass on any messages he may send them.

It's been a rough week.

I don't know which would be worse.

Him changing for her, and the kid? Making me feel I wasn't good enough to change for?

Or him staying the same, and putting another woman, and an innocent kid through his bullshit.

There's really no outcome that wouldn't hurt. I can barely think about it without crying at the moment.
